```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
A <- "docs/assets/fdr_panel10"
ov <- fread(file.path(A, "fdr_overview.tsv"))
vo <- fread(file.path(A, "overview_vs_original.tsv"))
rounds <- fread(file.path(A, "adaptive_rounds.tsv"))
cons <- fread(file.path(A, "consistency.tsv"))
g <- fread(file.path(A, "significant_genes.tsv"))
gc <- fread(file.path(A, "gene_changes.tsv"))
fmt <- function(n) format(n, big.mark=",", trim=TRUE, scientific=FALSE)
pct <- function(x, digits=0) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), 100 * x)
counts <- function(a, b) sprintf("%s (%s)", fmt(a), fmt(b))
any_tp <- ov[tp == "any timepoint"]; any_vo <- vo[tp == "any timepoint"]
fold <- function(gn, t) sprintf("%.1f", 2^g[gene == gn][[paste0("logFC_", t)]])
effect_reads <- function(d, t) fifelse(is.na(d[[paste0("dpsi_", t)]]), "no score",
  sprintf("%+.0f (%s)", 100 * d[[paste0("dpsi_", t)]], fmt(d[[paste0("het_cov_", t)]])))
best_q <- function(d) signif(pmin(d$q_bh_0hr, d$q_bh_1hr, d$q_bh_6hr, na.rm=TRUE), 2)
example_table <- function(genes, why) {
  d <- g[match(genes, gene)]
  data.table(Gene=d$gene, `0 hr`=effect_reads(d, "0hr"), `1 hr`=effect_reads(d, "1hr"), `6 hr`=effect_reads(d, "6hr"),
             `Best q`=best_q(d), `Het donors`=d$max_het, Relevance=why)
}
pattern_labels <- c("all three timepoints"="Significant at 3 timepoints",
                    "two timepoints"="Significant at 2 timepoints",
                    "shared, below threshold elsewhere"="One timepoint; nominal support elsewhere",
                    "candidate timepoint-specific"="One timepoint; no nominal support elsewhere",
                    "not testable elsewhere"="One timepoint; no usable score elsewhere")
g[, display_pattern := unname(pattern_labels[pattern])]
annot <- function(d) d[, .(`Neuronal GO term`=neuronal_go,
  `Developmental disorder or autism`=fifelse(nzchar(sfari) & nzchar(ddg2p), paste0(sfari, "; ", ddg2p), paste0(sfari, ddg2p)),
  `Expression after stimulation`=expression_response, `Splicing after stimulation`=fifelse(stim_splicing, "yes", ""))]
interactive_table <- function(d) DT::datatable(as.data.frame(d), rownames=FALSE, filter="top", extensions="Buttons",
  options=list(pageLength=10, lengthMenu=c(10, 25, 50), scrollX=TRUE, order=list(), dom="Blfrtip", buttons=c("copy", "csv")),
  caption="Search or filter genes, sort columns, and export the filtered table as CSV.")
all3 <- g[pattern == "all three timepoints"]
new_genes <- gc[status == "rerun only", gene]
```

This page repeats the [genome-wide FDR analysis](isolaser_fdr.html) with a
different way of choosing donors and associations. Many variant calls behind
the original results have no support in the donors' own genotype panel (see
[technical artifacts in isoLASER variant calls](isolaser_variant_artifacts.html)).
The original page and its results are unchanged.

**What changed (our definitions):**

- **Donors:** a donor is used for an association only if our genotype panel
  calls it heterozygous at that variant. The panel site must be directly
  genotyped or imputed with R² ≥ 0.8, with the same two alleles. The donor also
  needs ≥ 10 informative reads, isoLASER's own default. The original rule was
  ≥ 30 reads and an RNA alternative-allele fraction of 0.25–0.75.
- **Associations:** every variant × exonic part recorded in any donor. The
  original run used only the rows of isoLASER's joint output, which drops parts
  seen in a single donor.
- **Tested family:** additionally ≥ 20 raw reads summed over the donors used.
  Fewer can never give the ≥ 10 reads per allele that isoLASER needs to score
  an association.
- **Unchanged:** the shuffles, the scoring with isoLASER's functions, the
  adaptive rounds, BH within each timepoint, and the `cis` / |ΔPSI| ≥ 0.10
  screen applied afterwards.
- **Not yet done:** calibration runs. The original calibration used a
  different donor rule, so it does not carry over to this run.

**Main result:** `r fmt(any_tp$q05_associations)` associations in
**`r fmt(any_tp$q05_genes)` genes** have q < 0.05 and pass the screen,
against `r fmt(any_vo$original_q05_associations)` in
`r fmt(any_vo$original_q05_genes)` genes originally. `r nrow(all3)` genes are
significant at all three timepoints.

# Genome-wide results

```{r overview}
knitr::kable(ov[, .(Timepoint=tp, `Tested associations`=fmt(tested),
  `Paper's cutoff`=counts(paper_associations, paper_genes),
  Screen=counts(screen_associations, screen_genes),
  `Screen + q < 0.10`=counts(q10_associations, q10_genes),
  `Screen + q < 0.05`=counts(q05_associations, q05_genes))], align="lrrrrr")
```

Cells other than **Tested associations** show **associations (genes)**.

- **Paper's cutoff:** isoLASER's own `cis` call with no other filter, as in the
  isoLASER paper. It comes from isoLASER's joint output, so it is the same as on
  the original page.
- **Screen** (our definition), before FDR control: among the tested
  associations, isoLASER's `cis` rule computed on the panel-heterozygous donors
  only, plus |ΔPSI| ≥ 0.10.

**Any timepoint** counts each gene or variant–part association once across
timepoints. BH targets FDR within each timepoint's full family; the
effect-filtered subset and the union across timepoints have no separate 5% FDR
guarantee.

# Compared with the original run

```{r vs_original}
knitr::kable(vo[, .(Timepoint=tp,
  `Tested: original`=fmt(original_tested), `Tested: rerun`=fmt(tested),
  `Screen + q < 0.05: original`=counts(original_q05_associations, original_q05_genes),
  `Screen + q < 0.05: rerun`=counts(q05_associations, q05_genes))], align="lrrrr")
```

The rerun tests a similar number of associations, but far fewer reach
q < 0.05. Most original hits used variants that are not in the panel, which
the new donor rule cannot use.

# How the test works

The test is the one described on the [original page](isolaser_fdr.html#how-the-test-works).
Only the donor and family rules above differ. An association's eligible
donors are fixed before shuffling, from read counts and the panel genotype,
neither of which a shuffle changes. Eligible associations without a computable
observed score stay in the family with p = 1.

```{r rounds}
knitr::kable(rounds[, .(Timepoint=tp, `Stopped at 1,000`=fmt(stopped_1e3),
  `Stopped at 10,000`=fmt(stopped_1e4), `Stopped at 100,000`=fmt(stopped_1e5),
  `Reached 1,000,000`=fmt(reached_1e6))], align="lrrrr")
```

**Stopped** means at least 20 hits at that checkpoint, or no observed score
(p = 1). Every association with zero hits after a million shuffles has
q < 0.05, so more shuffles would not change the results.

![](assets/fdr_panel10/qq.png)

Real data only; there are no calibration runs for this donor rule. The bulk
lies below the diagonal: many associations tie with their shuffles at an AMI of
0, which isoLASER rounds to three decimals, so their p-values are
conservative. The upper plateau is the minimum attainable p-value.

# Genes to follow up

```{r follow_setup}
sashimi <- fread(file.path(A, "sashimi_summary.tsv"))
obs <- fread(file.path(A, "sashimi_observed_inclusion.tsv"))
sashimi_table <- function(gn) {
  d <- sashimi[gene == gn][order(timepoint)]
  frac <- function(i, e) sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", i, i + e, 100 * i / (i + e))
  knitr::kable(d[, .(Timepoint=sub("hr", " hr", timepoint), Donors=donors,
    `REF inclusion (raw)`=frac(REF_i, REF_e), `ALT inclusion (raw)`=frac(ALT_i, ALT_e),
    `Test dPSI (normalized, pp)`=sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * normalized_dPSI))], align="llrrr")
}
seen <- function(gn, t) { d <- obs[gene == gn & timepoint == t]
  sprintf("%s: %.0f%% vs %.0f%%", sub("hr", " hr", t), 100 * d[allele == "REF", seen_inclusion], 100 * d[allele == "ALT", seen_inclusion]) }
agree <- function(gn) { a <- tstrsplit(obs[gene == gn, agree], "/")
  sprintf("%s of %s", fmt(sum(as.integer(a[[1]]))), fmt(sum(as.integer(a[[2]])))) }
ob <- function(gn, t, a, x) obs[gene == gn & timepoint == t & allele == a][[x]]
n_two <- g[!grepl("0hr", sig_tps) & (neuronal | brain_disorder | stim_expression | stim_splicing), .N]
```

We highlight genes that meet three conditions (our definitions):

1. **Reported only after stimulation:** q < 0.05 plus the `cis` /
   effect-size screen at 1 or 6 hours, and not at 0 hours.
2. **Neuron- or stimulation-related:** a neuronal GO term, a brain disorder in
   SFARI or DDG2P, or a change in expression or splicing after stimulation in
   our data (the annotation columns of the full gene table below).
3. **Supported by the reads:** isoLASER calls a read "included" from the
   transcript the read is assigned to, not from what the read covers. A read
   *shows* the part if it has aligned bases inside it or a junction across it.
   Among the reads that show the part, the allelic difference must be visible.

`r n_two` genes meet the first two conditions; two of them also pass the read
check.

```{r highlight}
hl <- example_table(c("ZNF749", "PARK7"), c(
  "Splicing after stimulation (our scan), at this exon's donor sites",
  "Neuron projection, neuron death (GO); the Parkinson's disease gene DJ-1"))
hl[, `Reads that show the part` := c(seen("ZNF749", "6hr"), seen("PARK7", "1hr"))]
knitr::kable(hl, align="lrrrrrlr")
```

**0 / 1 / 6 hr**: allelic effect in percentage points, alternative minus
reference inclusion, with pooled informative coverage in brackets. **Best q**:
the lowest timepoint-specific q-value. **Het donors**: the largest number of
panel-heterozygous donors used, out of four. **Reads that show the part**:
inclusion among those reads at the significant timepoint, REF vs ALT.

**How to read each gene's figures:**

- **Permutation test:** one panel per timepoint. Grey bars are the first 1,000
  shuffled scores; the blue line is the observed score (AMI). The p-value uses
  the full adaptive run, up to a million shuffles.
- **Read alignments:** isoLASER's `nigiri_plot` sashimi renderer with the
  project's plotting fixes. Reads are split into REF (blue) and ALT (orange) by
  isoLASER's allele assignments and pooled over the donors used at each
  timepoint (heterozygous in the panel, ≥ 10 reads). Yellow marks the tested
  part. Coverage and arc numbers are raw read counts, on one scale per gene.
  **Raw inclusion** comes from transcript assignment; the test uses
  donor-normalized tables, so its dPSI can differ slightly.
- **Isoforms and haplotypes**, at 0 hours and at the significant timepoint,
  drawn like Fig. 2d of the isoLASER paper:
  - **Rows:** annotated transcripts with their GENCODE v44 name and Ensembl ID.
    **Novel** transcripts are IsoQuant models from our annotation, shown with
    their SQANTI3 category against GENCODE v44. NIC is a new combination of
    known splice sites; fusion spans two genes.
  - **Which rows:** the three transcripts with the most reads in each group are
    drawn, and a grey row sums the rest. Introns are shortened.
  - **Marks:** green is the tested part. Orange marks the tested SNP, plus the
    nearest in-phase SNP when that one is closer to the part.
  - **Numbers:** reads per transcript from each haplotype, labelled by the
    tested SNP's alleles, as raw counts summed over the donors used. ΔPSI and q
    are the test's values.

## ZNF749

The tested part is a 355-base alternative last exon. Transcripts that use it
end there, and the others continue to exons further downstream. REF (G) reads
end in it far more often than ALT (C) reads. The difference is significant only
at 6 hours (−74 pp, q = 0.002); at 0 and 1 hours it is −26 and −17 pp and below
threshold. In our stimulation splicing scan, the balance between the two donor
sites that splice into this exon shifts between 0 and 6 hours. Every read that
shows the exon agrees with isoLASER's call (`r agree("ZNF749")` over all
timepoints).

The jump at 6 hours partly reflects which donors are used:

- **CD_21** has a large effect at every timepoint: REF 92% vs ALT 15% inclusion
  at 0 hours, 86% vs 6% at 6 hours.
- **CD_48** shows no difference at 0 hours, from only 8 ALT reads, and a large
  one at 6 hours (85% vs 19%).
- **CD_36** has an inconsistent effect (−19 pp at 0 hours, +8 pp at 1 hour)
  and no reads at 6 hours.

One panel SNP lies inside the exon (chr19:57438167). It is heterozygous only
in CD_48, on that donor's REF haplotype. A mismatch there would push dPSI the
other way, so it does not explain the effect.

## PARK7

The first exon ends at one of two donor sites 58 bases apart, an alternative 5′
splice site, and both sites splice to the same next exon. The tested 12-base
part is the extra stretch of the longer first exon; the adjacent 46-base part
gives the same result. ALT (C) reads use the shorter exon more often than REF
(T) reads. The variant (rs226249) lies in the first exon, 18 bases before the
shorter exon's donor site.

The difference has the same direction at all three timepoints and in both
donors. It is largest at 1 hour (−17 pp, q = 0.002), the only significant
timepoint; at 0 and 6 hours it is −7 and −8 pp. This describes each timepoint
separately and is not a test of a change over time. Reads that show the part
agree with isoLASER's call in `r agree("PARK7")` cases.

## Checked and left out

The other genes that meet the first two conditions:

- **KPNA2** (synapse GO; 6 hours, +12 pp). No read shows the 100-base intron
  retained. At every timepoint, all reads that reach it splice it out: at
  6 hours, `r ob("KPNA2", "6hr", "REF", "skips")` REF and
  `r ob("KPNA2", "6hr", "ALT", "skips")` ALT reads. isoLASER's inclusion comes
  from reads assigned to KPNA2-221, the transcript that retains the intron; at
  6 hours, 20 of the 28 ALT reads assigned to it visibly splice the intron out.
  [Sashimi (PDF)](assets/fdr_panel10/KPNA2_sashimi.pdf).
- **ASAH1** (DDG2P; 1 hour, +21 pp). No read has aligned bases inside the
  part, and every read that reaches it splices across it. The 1-hour result
  also adds a second donor (CD_31) to the single donor used at 0 and 6 hours.
  [Sashimi (PDF)](assets/fdr_panel10/ASAH1_sashimi.pdf).
- **LMBRD1** (DDG2P; 1 and 6 hours). The variant is about 120 kb from the part.
  At 6 hours only 8 of 76 reads reach the part, and none includes it.
  [Sashimi (PDF)](assets/fdr_panel10/LMBRD1_sashimi.pdf).
- **ALDH3A2** (DDG2P; 1 hour). isoLASER did not record this association at 0
  or 6 hours, so there is no baseline to compare with.
- **UBE2Q2P2** (splicing after stimulation; 6 hours). A pseudogene, where reads
  from similar copies can be misaligned (our inference). Not checked against
  the reads.

Genes already reported at 0 hours are not highlighted here. Two we checked:

- **HNRNPK** passes the read check. Among reads that show its part, REF
  includes it `r sprintf("%.0f–%.0f%%", 100 * min(obs[gene == "HNRNPK" & allele == "REF", seen_inclusion]), 100 * max(obs[gene == "HNRNPK" & allele == "REF", seen_inclusion]))`
  of the time and ALT about 2%, at every timepoint.
- **CST3** fails it. Reads show its 13-base part included almost always for
  both alleles, but isoLASER's transcript-based inclusion is about 85% for REF
  and 27–31% for ALT. The ALT haplotype carries a second SNP inside the part
  (chr20:23637933 T>G), which most likely biases the transcript assignment
  (our inference).

# All reported genes

Here, **reported** means q < 0.05 plus the `cis` / effect-size screen.

```{r patterns}
pat <- g[, .N, by=pattern][match(names(pattern_labels), pattern)][!is.na(pattern)]
knitr::kable(pat[, .(Pattern=unname(pattern_labels[pattern]), Genes=N)], align="lr")
```

For genes reported at one timepoint, the last three categories describe the
representative association at the other timepoints: nominal p < 0.05,
p ≥ 0.05 where scored, or no usable score. They are not tests of an allele ×
time interaction. Among comparisons of significant associations with another
timepoint, `r pct(cons$nominal_p_lt_0.05)` had nominal p < 0.05 there and
`r pct(cons$same_sign)` had the same effect direction.

## Full interactive gene table

All **`r nrow(g)` reported genes**. The variant, part, timepoint effects, best q
and donor count refer to the representative association; **Significant at**
describes the gene across all its associations. **In original run** marks
genes also reported on the original page.

```{r all}
interactive_table(cbind(g[, .(Gene=gene, Pattern=display_pattern, `Significant at`=sig_tps,
  `0 hr`=effect_reads(g, "0hr"), `1 hr`=effect_reads(g, "1hr"), `6 hr`=effect_reads(g, "6hr"),
  `Best q`=best_q(g), `Het donors`=max_het,
  `In original run`=fifelse(gene %in% gc[status == "both", gene], "yes", "no"))], annot(g),
  g[, .(Variant=variant_qual, `Exonic part`=exonic_part)]))
```

The annotations use the same rules as on the
[original page](isolaser_fdr.html#full-interactive-gene-table). They help select
examples and are not enrichment tests.

**Data:** `10.isolaser_permutation/` with `ADAPTIVE_RULE=panel10`: inputs from
`38.prepare_panel_inputs.R`, then scripts 18–22 (see that folder's README). This
page's tables come from `11.fdr_results/3.page_tables.R` run with
`ADAPTIVE_RULE=panel10`, which writes only to `docs/assets/fdr_panel10/`.
